title: Copilot — Code Survival and Quality
description: Code survival rate metrics from VS OTel — measures how much AI-generated code developers actually keep. The most direct quality signal available in the pipeline.

options.content:
## Copilot Code Survival and Quality

Code survival metrics from Visual Studio OTel instrumentation. These are the most direct measure of AI code quality available in the pipeline — they measure whether developers actually keep the code Copilot generates.

**Two survival signals:**

| Metric | What it measures | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| **No-revert rate** | Percentage of AI edits that were NOT reverted by the developer | Higher is better — reverted code is code the developer rejected |
| **4-gram survival** | Percentage of 4-word code sequences from the AI suggestion that still exist in the file after a period of time | Higher means the code was kept and not substantially rewritten |

**Why this matters:** The GitHub API tells you how many lines were accepted (LOC Added). It does NOT tell you whether the developer kept that code or immediately reverted it. These OTel metrics close that gap — they are the truth signal on AI code quality.

**Note:** No user attribution — these are enterprise totals. Source metrics: `copilot_chat_edit_survival_no_revert_*` and `copilot_chat_edit_survival_four_gram_*`.

panels.title: No-Revert Rate
panels.description: Percentage of AI-generated code edits that were NOT reverted by developers. A higher rate means developers are keeping more of what Copilot generates. Target: above 70%. Below 50% indicates the model is producing code that developers frequently reject. Source: copilot_chat_edit_survival_no_revert.

panels.title: 4-Gram Survival Rate
panels.description: Percentage of 4-word code sequences from AI suggestions that still exist in the codebase after a review period. Higher means developers kept and did not substantially rewrite the AI code. This is a stronger quality signal than the no-revert rate because it measures long-term retention. Source: copilot_chat_edit_survival_four_gram.

panels.title: Total Edits Measured
panels.description: Total number of AI code edits for which survival was measured in the selected window. A larger sample gives higher confidence in the survival rate figures. Source: copilot_chat_edit_survival_no_revert_count.

panels.title: Total 4-Gram Samples
panels.description: Total number of 4-gram code sequence samples measured for survival in the selected window. Source: copilot_chat_edit_survival_four_gram_count.

panels.title: No-Revert Rate Over Time
panels.description: Daily no-revert rate trend. A rising rate indicates improving code quality or better developer-model fit over time. Dips may coincide with model changes, new feature rollouts, or shifts in the types of tasks developers are asking Copilot to help with.

panels.title: 4-Gram Survival Rate Over Time
panels.description: Daily 4-gram code survival rate trend. This is the strongest quality signal — it measures whether AI-generated code sequences persist in the codebase after developers have had time to review and modify them. A rising trend is the most meaningful indicator of improving AI code quality.

panels.title: No-Revert Rate by Model
panels.description: No-revert rate per model — which models produce code that developers keep most often. Use this to identify which models produce the highest quality output for your enterprise's codebase and use cases. A model with high token usage but low survival rate is expensive and low quality.

panels.title: 4-Gram Survival Rate by Model
panels.description: 4-gram code survival rate per model — which models produce code sequences that persist in the codebase longest. The model ranking here should guide model selection recommendations for code generation tasks where long-term code quality matters most.
